## How the guide reasons situationally

Named and argued in prose, one game at a time. The guide prints no situational database, no rest-differential column and no historical hit rate for any of these spots.

On 16 pages, and always attached to a specific game rather than stated as a system. Dustin Swedelson identifies Arkansas hosting Tulsa on September 26 as a dreaded lookahead spot with Texas A&M the following week; Aaron Moore builds a Clemson bet on a mid-September flight to Berkeley sitting between two heavyweight home games and three of the last four on the road. Sacramento State's Under cites midweek games and Midwest travel as practical burdens of the MAC move.

## The two things that are genuinely missing

**Weather.** Four incidental mentions across 345 pages. There is no systematic weather angle in this guide, and none is constructed here.

**Any measured travel figure.** Travel is named as a factor feeding home-field advantage on p. 21 and argued in prose where realignment bites, but no mileage, time-zone count or rest differential is printed anywhere.

## Where the measurable part lives

The one situational factor the guide does quantify is home-field advantage, and it does so per team rather than as a league constant — a home field rating and a road field rating for all 138 teams, which is what converts a power rating into a projected line. Those figures live in [`05_Power_Ratings`](../05_Power_Ratings/00_MAKINEN_RATINGS.md) and in every conference table.
